sharedRules.name: Panzerfaust - Limited 1
sharedRules.description:
Each time this Unit shoots, one of its Teams my shoot as a Panzerfaust rather than its usual weapons.
Each time this Unit rolls To Hit in an assault, one of its Teams may attack with a Panzerfaust rather than its usual weapons.

sharedRules.name: Bazooka Skirts
sharedRules.description: A Tank Team with Bazooka Skirts increases its Side armour to 5 against weapons with Firepower 5+ or 6.

sharedRules.name: Flame-thrower
sharedRules.description:
Infantry, Gun, and Unarmoured Tank Teams re-roll successful Saves when hit by a Flame-thrower and the Unit is automatically Pinned Down. Armoured Tank Teams use their Top armour for Armour Saves when hit by a Flame-thrower.

Flame-throwers my shoot in Defensive Fire. However, while a Unit that is Hit by a Flame-thrower is Pinned Down, this does not automatically stop the assault. The defender still needs to score five (or eight) hits to stop the assault as normal.

sharedRules.name: HEAT
sharedRules.description: A Team's Armour rating is not increased by +1 if it is more than 16"/40cm away when hit by HEAT weapons.

sharedRules.name: Mounted Assault
sharedRules.description: This Team has Assault 4+ and Counter attack 4+ with one Passenger and Assault 3+ and Counterattack 4+ with two or three Passengers. This is shown on the Transport Unit card as an additional motivation and skill column.

sharedRules.name: Stormtroopers
sharedRules.description: A unit may attempt a second Movement Order after succeeding in its first Movement Order. The second Movement Order must be different from the first.

sharedRules.name: Unit Transport
sharedRules.description: The Unit Leader of the Transport Attachment must end the Movement Step within 6"/15cm of the Unit Leader of its Passenger Unit while on the table. If it cannot do this, then the Transport Attachment must be Sent to the Rear. (see page 45 of the rulebook)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The elite crews of these Tiger tanks have learned many tricks on the Eastern Front.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
Before Deploying this Unit, roll a die and give this Unit the following command card at no additional point cost:
1: Clever Hans
2: Deadly Gunner
3: Rapid Fire
4: Schnell!
5: Roll Over Them
6: Choose one of the above

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Unit (Tiger Tank Company HQ, Tiger Tank Platoon)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: With a deadly gunner in your Tiger, every shot hits exactly where it’s aimed.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
The Unit Leader may re-roll one failed Firepower Test during the Shooting Step. 
*Use the Tiger Ace Skill card to get this card.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: It’s hard not to attract attention in agiant 56-tonne tank, but some crews have the knack. Smooth movement and staying to low ground can make even a Tiger tank hard to spot.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
This Unit gains the Scout rule.
Scout: Teams remain Gone to Ground whileMoving unless they Shoot or Assault. *Use the Tiger Ace Skill card to get this card.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: An ace gunner and an experienced loader allow a tank to engage and destroy numerous targets in a short span of time.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
The Unit Leader’s Tiger tank has Halted ROF 3 with its 8.8cm gun. 
*Use the Tiger Ace Skill card to get this card.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Most of their kills have been racked up through being in the right place at the right time!

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
This Unit passes Blitz Move tests on 2+. 
*Use the Tiger Ace Skill card to get this card.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: In a Tiger tank, it’s easy. You just roll over them. Keep moving and there’s nothing they can do to stop you.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
This Unit Leader’s Tiger tank hits in Assaults on 2+.
*Use the Tiger Ace Skill card to get this card.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text:
Hauptmann Fritz Adrario commanded the 200th and then the 272nd Anti-tank Battalions in Normandy. Under his command, the 200th scored 116 kills.
His experience as a reconnaissance commander in Russia underscored the need for anti-tank guns to open fire effectively from concealed positions.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text: Discard this card. If this 8.8cm Tank-hunter Platoon is Gone to Ground or being placed from Ambush, all Teams in this Unit may re-roll all failed rolls To Hit when targeting a Team more than 16"/40cm away.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Leutnant der Reserve Heinz Deutsch commanded the 3rd Company of the 12th Fallschirm StuG Battalion. He was awarded the Knight's Cross for knocking out 46 Allied tanks.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text: The Formation Commander may re-roll one failed roll To Hit each time he Shoots with his 7.5cm gun.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Formation, Warrior (Fallschirmjäger StuG Assault Gun Company) LFTF

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Leutnant Heinz Auert, commanded the 2nd Company of the 116th Reconnaissance Battalion. He had led reconnaissance troops aggressively since the Battle of France in 1940.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
Show this card to your opponent before Deployment.
If the Formation Commander of this Reconnaissance Company is Deployed on table, you may discard this card to roll a die immediately after Deployment. On a score of 3+, this player has the first turn, but the rules for a Meeting Engagement (page 104 of the rulebook) apply to all Teams in this Force not in this Formation. Teams in this Force cannot be Dug In or Gone to Ground at the end of their first turn.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Oberstleutnant Hermann Dropmann led the 1050th Grenadier Regiment of the 77th Infantry Division in Normandy. In close combat on 4 July, he personally knocked out five American tanks, bringing his tally to nine, and earning a Knight's Cross.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
In Assaults, the Formation Commander Hits on a roll of 3+. Tanks that he Hits will Save using their Top Armour against his Anti-tank rating of 4.
The Formation HQ and any Unit that is making a combined Assault with it Counterattack on a roll of 3+.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Formation, Warrior (Beach Defence Grenadier Company)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Dispite his rebellious goatee and shaggy hair, Unteroffizier Kurt Knispel, refused abandon anyone on the field of battle, even in the worst of situations and conditions. Fighting as a tank commander in the 1st Company of the 503rd Heavy Tank Battalion, he was awarded the German Cross in Gold for 168 tank kills and 70 anti-tank guns destroyed, Germany's highest scoring ace.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
The Unit Leader may re-roll all failed rolls To Hit each time he Shoots with his 8.8cm gun.
This Unit automatically passes all Last Stand tests.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Leutnant der Reserve Wilhelm Bäder had fought in both Russia and Tunisia in the artillery of the 10th Panzer Division. Posted to the 363rd Infantry Division, he first commanded infantry guns, then a rifle company earnings in the Knight's Cross.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text: The Formation Commander successfully Ranges In any Artillery Unit from his Formation on a 3+. Whenever he successfully Ranges In an Artillery Unit from his Formation, he may immediately roll to Range In another Artillery Unit from his Formation. If successful, the additional Artillery Unit is treated as Ranging In on the same attempt.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Formation, Warrior (Beach Defence Grenadier Company)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Some men have all the luck.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text: Discard this card to re-roll any one die. The second result must be used.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Coastal defence divisions spent more of their time building fortifications and laying minefields than training to clear them. Despite this, they had more training in doing so than the average soldier.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
Infantry Teams in this Unit cross Minefields safely on a roll of 3+.
This Unit Digs In on a roll of 3+.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Unit (Beach Defence Grenadier Platoon)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Every panzer division had pioneers whose role was to clear the way for assaults, breaching minefields and clearing other obstacles.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
Infantry Teams in this Unit cross Minefields safely on a roll of 2+.
This Unit Digs In on a roll of 2+.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Unit (Armoured Panzergrenadier Platoon, Panzergrenadier Platoon)

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
If the Unit Leader did not Move, discard this card to pick an enemy Infantry or Gun Team in Bulletproof Cover, up to 12"/30cm away from, and in Line of Sight of the Unit Leader. Roll a Skill test for the Unit Leader instead of Shooting:
- If passed, the enemy Team is Hit with a Firepower 3+ weapon and their Unit is Pinned Down. Infantry or Gun Teams must re-roll successful Saves.
If the line between the Unit Leader and the enemy Team crosses Terrain more than 2"/5cm from the enemy Team, roll a die for each item of terrain. Any roll that is not 4+ causes the attack to miss. If the line crosses any Impassable Terrain, the attack misses.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Unit (Pioneer Platoon, Panzer Pioneer Platoon)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: In Normandy, the location of minefields was poorly recorded or lost, creating a hazard for troops moving through No-Man's Land.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
Before Objectives are placed, place five Old Minefield markers. The players alternate placing markers, starting with this player. Markers must be placed in No-Man's Land or this Force's Deployment Area, and at least 4"/10cm apart.
When a Team moves within 2"/5cm of an Old Minefield marker, roll a die. On a score of 4+, remove the Old Minefield marker. Otherwise, replace the Old Minefield marker with a Minefield Marker and tests for entering a Minefield as normal.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The Allied Air Forces experimented with carpet bombing. In theory the heavy bombers would flatten everything. In practice, it wasn't as effective as expected -- and the bombs tended to land on the assault troops as well, delaying their advance.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text: Discard this card after your opponent rolls for Reserves. Your opponent must re-roll their Reserves rolls.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The 217th Assault Tank Battalion supported both infantry and panzer divisions against the British offensives in August 1944. They were useful in counterattacks against villages lost in the battle for the Falaise Pocket.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text: You may field a Brummbär Assault Tank Platoon (LG133) (at the cost shown on the card) in place of a Jagdpanzer IV Tank Hunter Platoon.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: On D-Day, the 2nd 'Vienna' Panzer Division was the best equipped and trained division in the entire German Army. Faced with overwhelming firepower, they quickly learned that night operations were more survivable.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
If this Force is the attacker in a mission where the defender has Minefields, you may attack at night. If you do so, Night Fighting rules (see page 113 of the rulebook) are in effect at the start of the game.
Units from this Formation can move freely from the start of the game. Friendly Units from other Formations or Support may not move out of their Deployment Area until morning breaks.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The remnants of the 9th Panzer Division had been fighting in Southern Russia just a month before D-Day. With little time to rebuild, and none to train the soldiers replacing the veterans lost on the Eastern Front, they were thrown back into battle.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
All Units in this Formation have a Tactics rating of 4+ for -1 point per Unit.
Skill: Tactics 4+

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Formation (any Tank or Panzergrenadier Company), Title

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Ordered to counterattack the American breakthrough at Mortain, the newly-rebuilt 116th Panzer Division performed well as the rearguard at Falaise.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
All Units in this Formation lose Third Reich, and have a Last Stand rating of 5+ and a Tactics rating of 4+ for -1 points per Unit. (LFTF)
Motivation: Last Stand 5+
Skill: Tactics 4+

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Formation (any Tank or Panzergrenadier Company), Title

sharedSelectionEntries.name: Air Force Soldiers, 16th Luftwaffe Field Division

profiles.name: Air Force Soldiers, 16th Luftwaffe Field Division

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: In 1942, the Luftwaffe (the German Air Force) formed 20 weak infantry divisions from unneeded ground crew. They were politically motivated, but they lacked infantry training, although their high level of education allowed them to pick up tricks quickly.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
The HQ Unit and all Beach Defence Grenadier Platoons in this Formation have the following ratings for +1 point per Unit:
Motivation: 4+, Counterattack 3+, Last Stand 5+
Skill: 5+, Tactics 4+

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Formation (Beach Defence Grenadier Company), Title

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The 352nd Infantry Division was formed from the devastated remains of the 321st Infantry Divisions which was destroyed defending Bryansk after the Battle of Kursk. Led by a handful of 'Front Swine' who had learned their trade in the mud of the Eastern Front, they fought hard to hold what they had.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
The HQ Unit and all Beach Defence Grenadier Platoons in this Formation have the following ratings for +1 point per Unit:
Motivation: 4+, Last Stand 5+, Rally 3+
Skill: 5+, Assault 4+

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Formation (Beach Defence Grenadier Company), Title

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The 30th Fast Brigade was the Seventh Army's mobile reserve. Mounted on bicycles and close behind the front, they were able to quickly reinforce the 352nd Infantry Division where they were desperately needed.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
Discard this card after rolling for Reserves to re-roll all of your Reserve rolls.
All Reserves arriving this turn must be from this Beach Defence Grenadier Company.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Formation (Beach Defence Grenadier Company), Title

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Major Messerschmidt's assault battalion counter attacked the American airborne landings at Saint-Mere-Eglise, then fought its way back to defend the port of Cherbourg.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
The HQ Unit and all Beach Defence Grenadier Platoons in this Formation have the following ratings for +2 points per Unit:
Motivation: 4+
Skill: 4+, Assault 3+

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Formation (Beach Defence Grenadier Company), Title

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Desperately short of soldiers, the German Army recruited Osttruppen from prisoners of war captured on the Eastern Front (Ostfront). While potentially unreliable, they freed up troops for more important tasks than guarding potential invasion beaches.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
All Beach Defence Grenadier Platoons in this Formation have the following ratings:
Motivation: 5+
Skill: 5+

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Formation (Beach Defence Grenadier Company), Title

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The veteran 2nd Fallschirmjäger Division had suffered badly as it attempted to halt the Red Army's advance across the Ukraine. It had barely arrived in Germany for rebuilding when it was sent to hold the port of Brest along with a motley assortment of second line troops. The division's aggressive raids kept the besieging American forces at bay.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
Replace one Fallschirmjäger Platoon in this Formation with a Beach Defence Grenadier Platoon.
Fallschirmjäger Platoons in this Formation have the Spearhead rule, but only Fallschirmjäger Units may deploy in the Spearhead extension to their Deployment Area.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Only one-in-ten of the 5th Fallschirmjäger Division had completed jump training, and many of their ex-Air Force officers had no infantry training, by the time they were sent into battle. Despite this, they fought bravely.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
The HQ and all Fallschirmjäger Rifle Platoons in this Formation have the following ratings for -1 point per Unit:
Motivation: 3+
Skill: 4+

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Major Friedrich von der Heydte's 6th Fallschirmjäger Regiment was in action against American paratroopers on D-Day and fought until the end of the campaign, surviving despite being trapped in two pockets.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text: Any Unit from this Fallschirmjäger Company whose Unit Leader is within 6"/15cm of the Formation Commander has a Last Stand rating of 2+.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Some of the infantry divisions in Normandy had been hastily formed, and lacked the desired level of training and experience.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
All 10.5cm Artillery Batteries in this Force have the following ratings for -1 point per Gun team:
Motivation: 4+, Last Stand 5+
Skill: 4+, Assault 6
Is Hit On: 3+

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Formation (Beach Defence Grenadier Company), Title

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Despite its hasty raising and general shortage of equipment, the artillery regiment of the 77th Infantry Division included a battalion of powerful 8.8cm anti-tank guns.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
All 8.8cm Tank-hunter Platoons in this Force have the following ratings for -1 point per Gun team:
Motivation: 4+, Last Stand 5+
Skill: 4+, Assault 6
Is Hit On: 3+

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Formation (Beach Defence Grenadier Company), Title

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The shortage of German equipment meant that formations like the 265th Infantry Division had to make do with captured Russian guns.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
This Force must field 76mm Artillery or 122mm Artillery Batteries (LS148 or LS149) (at the cost shown on the card) in place of 10.5cm Artillery Batteries, with the following ratings:
Motivation: 4+, Last Stand 5+
Skill: 4+, Assault 6
Is Hit On: 3+

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Formation (Beach Defence Grenadier Company), Title

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Tank brigades formed specialist SMG companies to ride on their tanks and protect them from enemy tank hunters.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text: Infantry teams from the Fallschirmjäger Rifle Platoon or Beach Defence Grenadier Platoon from within this Formation can Shoot while Mounted on Armoured Tank teams from this Formation (to a maximum of one team per Tank), and can Dismount when Charging into Contact.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Formation (Fallschirmjäger StuG Assault Gun Company)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: By 1944 many of the self-propelled anti-aircraft units were armoured to protect them from small arms fire and shrapnel.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
All Sd Kfz 10/4 (2cm) or Sd Kfz 7/1 (Quad 2cm) tanks in this Unit have the following Armour rating instead of their normal Unarmoured Tank Save:
Armour:
Front: 0
Side & Rear: 0
Top: 0

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Unit, (Sd Kfz 10/4 Light AA Platoon, Sd Kfz 7/1 Quad AA Platoon)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: German infantry dug camouflaged nests for their heavy machine-guns, covering them with soil mounted over doors and beams stolen from wrecked French houses.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
sMG34 or sMG42 HMG teams in this Unit cannot Move, but can rotate to face the target when Shooting, and are Nests. 
Each HMG team is a separate Independent Team.
Nests: The Nests are always Concealed and in Bulletproof Cover.
Teams attacking a Nest must re-roll successful Firepower tests to Destroy it.
Nests cannot Charge into Contact.
MG Nests do not use the Beach Defences rules from the D-Day: American book. (LFTF)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The German defences featured carefully camouflaged anti-tank gun nests. The guns would wait until the enemy tanks were in the killing zone, then open fire.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
Gun teams in this Unit cannot Move, but can rotate to face the target when shooting, and are Nests.
Each Gun team is a separate Independent Team.
Nest: The Nests are always Concealed and in Bulletproof Cover.
Teams attacking a Nest must re-roll successful Firepower tests to Destroy it.
Nests cannot Charge into Contact.
(LFTF: This card can be used with any Gun Unit, including artillery and anti-aircraft guns. Units using this card cannot fire Artillery Bombardments or shoot at Aircraft. Pakfront Nests do not use the Beach Defences rules from the D-Day: American book. This costs +2 points per Gun team, rather than +6 points for the Unit.)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: When its attempts to push the British back into the sea failed, Rommel's 21st Panzer Division dug in a line of Panzer IV tanks as anti-tank guns to back up the defending infantry.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
Panzer IV tanks in this Unit are Concealed and cannot Move, but can rotate its turret to face the target when Shooting.
Treat all Hits on these tanks as being on their turret when determining whether to use Front or Side armour.
If placed from Ambush, they must be more than 16"/40cm from all enemy Teams within Line of Sight.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.$text: German, Build, Unit (Panzer IV Tank Platoon), Limited

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: As their losses increased, the Germans started using captured Allied equipment.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
You may field one M5 Stuart (LU103) for 3 points, one M8 Greyhound (LU174) for 2 points, one Sherman (LB102) for 4 points, or one Firefly (LB103) for 5 points, as a Looted Tank.
The Looted Tank has a Moving ROF of 1 for any 75mm or 37mm guns, and is an Independant Team with the following ratings:
Motivation: 4+
Skill: 4+
Is Hit On: 3+

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The divisions rebuilding in Normandy were issued the latest Puma and Sd Kfz 234 eight-wheeled armoured cars.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
Your Force includes one Puma Scout Company, which is a Formation containing:
- 1 HQ Unit of 1x Puma (5cm) armoured car from (LG178) for 2 points, or 1x Sd Kfz 234 (2cm) armoured car (LG178) for 1 point.
- 2-12 Puma Scout Troop (LG178)
- 0-2 Sd Kfz 234 (7.5cm) Gun Platoon (LG188)
- 0-1 Reconnaissance Platoon (LG174)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Small and agile Sd Kfz 250 half-tracked armoured cars replaced the light four wheeled types of earlier years in the panzer division reconnaissance battalions.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
Your Force includes one Half-track Scout Company, which is a Formation containing:
- 1 HQ Unit of 1x Sd Kfz 250 (MG) half-track from (LG179) for 1 point.
- 2-8 Sd Kfz 250 Scout Troop (LG179)
- 0-2 Sd Kfz 234 (7.5cm) Gun Platoon (LG188)
- 0-1 Reconnaissance Platoon (LG174)

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The vast majority of additional artillery support available to German divisions in Normandy came from the three Nebelwerfer rocket launcher brigades. As a result, Allied soldiers came to hate the 'Screaming Meemies'.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text: You may field a 15cm Nebelwerfer Battery (LG137) in place of a 10.5cm Artillery Battery (LG136). This allows you to field two 15cm Nebelwerfer Batteries.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The 3rd Flak Corps had a dual role, fighting as both heavy anti-aircraft guns and as heavy anti-tank guns.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
All 8.8cm Heavy AA Platoons in this Force have the following ratings for -1 point per Gun team:
Motivation: 4+, Last Stand 5+
Skill: 5+, Assault 6
Is Hit On: 3+

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The 1039th Anti-tank Artillery Battalion had a dual mission, operating as long-range artillery when it wasn't needed for anti-tank defence.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
This 8.8cm Tank-hunter Platoon may fire an Artillery Bombardment with the following characteristics:
Weapon: 8.8cm gun
Range: 88"/220cm
ROF: ARTILLERY
Anti-Tank: 2
Fire-power: 4+

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The small Sd Kfz 250 half-track was used as an artillery observation post. It's small size allowed it to avoid unwanted attention.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text: Replace the Panzer III OP with an Sd Kfz 250 OP (see back of card).

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The divisions training in France had a low priority for trucks and other transport, while the costal defence divisions had almost none! Despite this, some units managed to scrape together enough vehicles to motorise at least part of their guns and infantry.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
This Infantry or Gun Unit may add a Softskin Transport Attachment. The number of vehicles in the Unit is as follows:
- Add one Softskin Transport for every two Infantry Teams in the Unit
- Add one Softskin Transport for each Gun Team in the Unit.
The characteristics of a Softskin Transport are shown on the back of this card.
